ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graphs of the functions $y=ax+b$ and $y=kx$ intersect at point $P$. According to the graph, what is the solution set of the linear inequality in one variable $ax+b>kx$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the graph of the function indicates that when $x>-3$, the linear function $y=ax+b$ is above the graph of the linear function $y=kx$, \\
therefore, the solution to the inequality in $x$, $ax+b>kx$, is $\boxed{x>-3}$.

Observing the image, it can be seen that on the right side of the intersection point P, the straight line y=ax+b is above the straight line y=kx; on the left side of the intersection point P, the straight line y=ax+b is below y=kx. method.method_draft: First read the graph: point P is the intersection of the two lines, and the dashed vertical from P meets the x-axis at x = -3. The line labeled y = ax + b lies above the line labeled y = kx to the right of P, while to the left of P it lies below. From the text, the inequality ax + b > kx asks for x-values where the graph of y = ax + b is vertically higher than the graph of y = kx. Therefore select the right side of the intersection, giving x > -3.

method.method_draft: First read the graph: the two lines cross at P, whose x-coordinate is -3, so ax + b = kx when x = -3. Also from the graph, y = ax + b has positive slope and y = kx has negative slope, so the difference (ax + b) - kx increases as x increases. Since this difference is 0 at x = -3, it is positive for x-values greater than -3 and negative for x-values less than -3. Thus the solution to ax + b > kx is x > -3.
